checks.requirement: Prohibition of AI systems that manipulate behavior, exploit vulnerabilities, or perform social scoring by public authorities
checks.rationale: The system does not engage in social scoring (confirmed as 'no'), does not manipulate human behavior, and is deployed in employment context by private entities for CV screening, not for prohibited public authority social scoring purposes.
checks.source_citation: Article 5 prohibits AI practices including social scoring by public authorities and systems that manipulate human behavior to cause harm or exploit vulnerabilities based on age, disability or socio-economic situation.

checks.requirement: Training, validation and testing data shall be subject to appropriate data governance and management practices
checks.rationale: The questionnaire confirms data governance measures are in place ('yes'). For an employment screening system handling CVs, this indicates structured data management practices are implemented to ensure data quality and relevance.
checks.source_citation: Article 10 requires that training, validation and testing data sets shall be subject to appropriate data governance and management practices, including examination for possible biases and appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases.

checks.requirement: Technical documentation shall be drawn up and kept up to date to demonstrate compliance with requirements
checks.rationale: Technical documentation is marked as 'partial', indicating incomplete documentation. For a high-risk employment AI system making automated decisions affecting fundamental rights, comprehensive technical documentation is mandatory to demonstrate compliance.
checks.remediation: Complete all technical documentation including system design specifications, data governance procedures, risk management measures, testing and validation results, and human oversight mechanisms. Ensure documentation is maintained and updated throughout the system lifecycle.
checks.source_citation: Article 11 mandates that technical documentation shall be drawn up before the high-risk AI system is placed on the market or put into service and shall be kept up-to-date, demonstrating that the AI system complies with the requirements set out in this Regulation.

checks.requirement: High-risk AI systems shall be designed with automatic recording capabilities to ensure traceability throughout their lifecycle
checks.rationale: While the system has human oversight and data governance, there is no explicit confirmation of comprehensive logging and record-keeping capabilities. For automated CV screening decisions, audit trails of system outputs and decision-making processes are essential.
checks.remediation: Implement automatic logging of all screening decisions, candidate rankings, input data used, timestamps, and any human interventions. Ensure logs are retained for appropriate periods and are accessible for auditing and compliance verification.
checks.source_citation: Article 12 requires high-risk AI systems to be designed and developed with capabilities enabling the automatic recording of events (logs) throughout the system's lifecycle, ensuring a level of traceability appropriate to the intended purpose of the system.

checks.requirement: High-risk AI systems shall be designed to be sufficiently transparent to enable users to interpret outputs and use them appropriately
checks.rationale: Transparency measures are confirmed as implemented ('yes'). This suggests that HR users receive interpretable outputs from the CV screening system, enabling them to understand candidate rankings and make informed decisions.
checks.source_citation: Article 13 mandates that high-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable users to interpret the system's output and use it appropriately.

checks.requirement: High-risk AI systems shall be designed with appropriate human oversight measures to prevent or minimize risks to health, safety or fundamental rights
checks.rationale: Human oversight is confirmed as present ('yes'). For employment screening affecting fundamental rights to work and non-discrimination, human review of automated CV rankings ensures that final hiring decisions involve human judgment and accountability.
checks.source_citation: Article 14 requires high-risk AI systems to be designed and developed in such a way that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which the AI system is in use, with measures including human-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop, or human-in-command approaches.

checks.requirement: High-risk AI systems shall achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle
checks.rationale: Accuracy testing is marked as 'partial', indicating incomplete validation of the system's performance. For CV screening systems that must avoid discriminatory outcomes and ensure fair candidate evaluation, comprehensive accuracy and bias testing is critical.
checks.remediation: Conduct comprehensive accuracy testing including validation against diverse candidate profiles, bias testing across protected characteristics (gender, age, ethnicity, disability), robustness testing with varied CV formats, and regular performance monitoring post-deployment. Document all testing methodologies and results.
checks.source_citation: Article 15 mandates that high-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, and perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle.

checks.requirement: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall ensure transparency and provide information to downstream providers
checks.rationale: The system is confirmed as not being a general-purpose AI model ('gpai_model': 'no'). Article 50 transparency requirements apply specifically to GPAI models, not to specialized employment screening systems.
checks.source_citation: Article 50 applies to providers of general-purpose AI models, requiring them to draw up and keep up to date technical documentation and make it available to the AI Office and national competent authorities.

checks.requirement: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk shall perform model evaluation, adversarial testing, and track serious incidents
checks.rationale: The system does not present systemic risk ('systemic_risk': 'no') and is not a general-purpose AI model. Article 51 obligations apply only to GPAI models with systemic risk, which is not applicable to this specialized CV screening system.
checks.source_citation: Article 51 imposes additional obligations on providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, including performing model evaluations, conducting adversarial testing, and tracking and reporting serious incidents.
